title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
subtitle: Classic garlic and olive oil pasta
excerpt: Five ingredients, fifteen minutes, and a proper Italian weeknight staple. The trick is gently frying the garlic in plenty of olive oil without letting it colour too dark.
sourceNotes: Traditional Neapolitan recipe. Chilli flakes and parsley are the only additions to the canonical garlic-oil base.

content.text: Keep the pasta water starchy and use it to bring the sauce together. The garlic goes in cold oil so it cooks slowly without burning.
Bring a large pan of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the spaghetti according to packet instructions until just al dente.
While the pasta cooks, put the garlic and olive oil in a cold frying pan. Place over low-medium heat. Cook gently for 6 to 8 minutes until the garlic is pale gold and fragrant.
Add the chilli flakes. Stir for 30 seconds.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Drain the pasta and add it to the frying pan. Add a large splash of pasta water. Toss over medium heat for 1 minute until the sauce clings to the pasta.
Remove from the heat. Add the parsley and toss again. Serve with parmesan if using.

items.symptom: Garlic turned dark brown and bitter.
items.cause: Heat was too high or it was left unattended.
items.fix: Start again with fresh garlic in cold oil over low heat.

items.cause: Not enough pasta water added to emulsify the oil.
items.fix: Add more pasta water a splash at a time while tossing.

items.symptom: Dish tastes flat despite the garlic.
items.cause: Pasta was not salted enough during cooking.
items.fix: Add flaky salt at the table and use more next time.
